g.aria-label: Title text 'Figure 14: Whether CAMS aerosol helps in cloud-free and dusty hours'

text.font-family: Matter XH, DM Sans, sans-serif

g.text: Figure 14: Whether CAMS aerosol helps in cloud-free and dusty hours

g.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Six NGED solar farms, daylight hours, September 2019 to December 2025. ERA5: ECMWF's reanalysis of past weather. CAMS: satellite irradiance service. Dot: estimate. Line: 95% interval from resampling whole months. Main XGBoost tuning setting. Dashed rules: no difference, and (on the error panels) the smallest improvement worth acting on (0.1 percentage points). Labels give distinct days (d) and months (mo). A row is assessed only with at least 20 days in 12 months. Aerosol: optical depth from CAMS's EAC4 reanalysis (a CAMS global atmosphere record). Clear: ERA5 total cloud cover below 0.2. Dusty: dust optical depth in the top 5% of hours. Clean: total aerosol optical depth below its median. CRPS scores the whole predicted distribution; error is the mean absolute error. A reanalysis knows the dust plume, so a forecast would gain less. A variable set is the list of inputs the XGBoost model is given. G0: sun position, ERA5 solar radiation (ssrd), and air temperature (t2m). Each group adds to the one before. G1: total cloud cover. G2: low, mid, and high cloud cover. G3: clear-sky radiation. G4: cloud water and cloud base height. G5: direct beam. G6: wind and thermal radiation. G7: humidity and haze. G8: snow and albedo. G9 (the full set): all other ERA5 variables. G10: G9 plus CAMS aerosol. Clearness index: irradiance divided by the irradiance at the top of the atmosphere. Exploratory: not named in the study plan before any result existed, and not corrected for multiple comparisons.'

text.font-family: Matter XH, DM Sans, sans-serif
text.tspan: Six NGED solar farms, daylight hours, September 2019 to December 2025. ERA5: ECMWF's reanalysis of past weather.
Dot: estimate. Line: 95% interval from resampling whole months. Main XGBoost tuning
setting. Dashed rules: no difference, and (on the error panels) the smallest
improvement worth acting on (0.1 percentage points). Labels give distinct days (d)
and months (mo). A row is assessed only with at least 20 days in 12 months.
Aerosol: optical depth from CAMS's EAC4 reanalysis (a CAMS global atmosphere record).
Clear: ERA5 total cloud cover below 0.2. Dusty: dust optical depth in the top 5% of
hours. Clean: total aerosol optical depth below its median. CRPS scores the whole
predicted distribution; error is the mean absolute error.
A reanalysis knows the dust plume, so a forecast would gain less.
A variable set is the list of inputs the XGBoost model is given. G0: sun position, ERA5 solar
radiation (ssrd), and air temperature (t2m). Each group adds to the one before.
G1: total cloud cover. G2: low, mid, and high cloud cover. G3: clear-sky radiation.
G4: cloud water and cloud base height. G5: direct beam. G6: wind and thermal radiation.
G7: humidity and haze. G8: snow and albedo. G9 (the full set): all other ERA5 variables.
Clearness index: irradiance divided by the irradiance at the top of the atmosphere.
Exploratory: not named in the study plan before any result existed, and not corrected for multiple comparisons.
